title: Habitat fragmentation and edge effects
caption: The same area of habitat as one block or as four small patches. Fragmenting it turns interior habitat into edge: the proportion of core habitat falls from about 63% to about 33%, although the habitat area is the same, and the patches are isolated. A narrow corridor joins the patches again, though corridor cells are all edge. An illustrative grid, not a real landscape.
alt: Three small maps. One block of 96 habitat cells with a large dark core; the same 96 cells split into four patches, most of them now edge; and the four patches joined by narrow corridors into one connected patch.
description: One block of habitat has a large core and a small share of edge.
The same area split into four patches is mostly edge: edge effects (light, temperature, wind and predators) reach most of it, so species that need the interior decline.
Corridors reconnect the patches, but they are all edge and add only a little habitat.
Illustrative grid: 96 habitat cells in each of the first two maps.
